rules.title: Annual allowable rent increase
rules.requirement: Landlords may impose the allowable percentage rent increase once every 12 months.
rules.key_value: Once every 12 months; percentage not supplied
rules.coverage_conditions: Los Angeles rental properties generally covered by the RSO: first built on or before October 1, 1978, or replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28, with one of the listed types: apartment, condominium, townhome, duplex, two or more single-family dwellings on the same parcel, hotel/motel/rooming-house/boarding-house rooms occupied by the same tenant for more than 30 consecutive days, residential units attached to commercial buildings, ADUs or JADUs. Mobile homes and recreational vehicles in mobile home parks are also covered. Rent regulation excludes condominium and townhome tenancies commencing after December 31, 1995. Applicable RSO exemptions must be resolved, including the incompletely described luxury and temporary exemptions.
rules.exemptions: This is the ordinary allowable percentage increase. The overview separately describes market-rate resets, additional-tenant increases, surcharges and increases requiring LAHD approval; their interaction with this frequency restriction is not fully stated.
rules.citation: City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO)

rules.title: No additional percentage increase for utilities
rules.requirement: Landlords may no longer include an additional percentage rent increase for utilities.
rules.coverage_conditions: Los Angeles rental properties generally covered by the RSO: first built on or before October 1, 1978, or replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28, with one of the listed types: apartment, condominium, townhome, duplex, two or more single-family dwellings on the same parcel, hotel/motel/rooming-house/boarding-house rooms occupied by the same tenant for more than 30 consecutive days, residential units attached to commercial buildings, ADUs or JADUs. Mobile homes and recreational vehicles in mobile home parks are also covered. Rent regulation excludes condominium and townhome tenancies commencing after December 31, 1995. Applicable RSO exemptions must be resolved, including the incompletely described luxury and temporary exemptions.
rules.exemptions: The stated prohibition concerns an additional percentage increase for utilities.
rules.citation: City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO)
rules.quoted_span: Effective February 2, 2026, the landlord can no longer include an additional percentage increase for utilities.

rules.title: No additional dependent increase
rules.requirement: Landlords may no longer impose an additional 10% rent increase for an additional dependent added to the tenancy.
rules.coverage_conditions: Los Angeles rental properties generally covered by the RSO: first built on or before October 1, 1978, or replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28, with one of the listed types: apartment, condominium, townhome, duplex, two or more single-family dwellings on the same parcel, hotel/motel/rooming-house/boarding-house rooms occupied by the same tenant for more than 30 consecutive days, residential units attached to commercial buildings, ADUs or JADUs. Mobile homes and recreational vehicles in mobile home parks are also covered. Rent regulation excludes condominium and townhome tenancies commencing after December 31, 1995. Applicable RSO exemptions must be resolved, including the incompletely described luxury and temporary exemptions.
rules.exemptions: The source distinguishes an additional dependent from an additional tenant who is not a dependent. It does not define dependent.
rules.citation: City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO)
rules.quoted_span: Effective February 2, 2026, an additonal 10% increase for an additional dependent added to the tenancy is no longer permitted. However, a 10% for an additional tenant is allowed (not a dependent) if moves into a rental unit: Landlords can increase the rent within 60 days of learning about the additional tenant.

rules.title: Additional nondependent tenant increase
rules.requirement: When an additional tenant who is not a dependent moves into a rental unit, the landlord may increase rent by 10% within 60 days of learning about that tenant.
rules.key_value: 10%; within 60 days of learning of the additional tenant
rules.coverage_conditions: Los Angeles rental properties generally covered by the RSO: first built on or before October 1, 1978, or replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28, with one of the listed types: apartment, condominium, townhome, duplex, two or more single-family dwellings on the same parcel, hotel/motel/rooming-house/boarding-house rooms occupied by the same tenant for more than 30 consecutive days, residential units attached to commercial buildings, ADUs or JADUs. Mobile homes and recreational vehicles in mobile home parks are also covered. Rent regulation excludes condominium and townhome tenancies commencing after December 31, 1995. This particular allowance is limited to an additional tenant who is not a dependent moving into the unit. Applicable RSO exemptions must be resolved, including the incompletely described luxury and temporary exemptions.
rules.exemptions: Dependents do not qualify. For unauthorized additional tenants who moved between March 2020 and December 2023, the source requires advance written notice of the increase on or before March 1, 2024; it does not establish a new notice opportunity after that deadline.
rules.citation: City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO)
rules.quoted_span: Effective February 2, 2026, an additonal 10% increase for an additional dependent added to the tenancy is no longer permitted. However, a 10% for an additional tenant is allowed (not a dependent) if moves into a rental unit: Landlords can increase the rent within 60 days of learning about the additional tenant. Rent increases for unauthorized additional tenants who moved between March 2020 and December 2023 must be provided an advance written notice of rental increase on or before March 1, 2024.

rules.title: Specified grounds for a market-rate reset
rules.requirement: Landlords may increase rent to market rate when the tenant voluntarily moves out, accepts a Tenant Buyout Agreement, or is evicted for nonpayment, a lease violation, failure to comply with a Tenant Habitability Plan, or a City Attorney order.
rules.key_value: Market rate following a listed trigger
rules.coverage_conditions: Los Angeles rental properties generally covered by the RSO: first built on or before October 1, 1978, or replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28, with one of the listed types: apartment, condominium, townhome, duplex, two or more single-family dwellings on the same parcel, hotel/motel/rooming-house/boarding-house rooms occupied by the same tenant for more than 30 consecutive days, residential units attached to commercial buildings, ADUs or JADUs. Mobile homes and recreational vehicles in mobile home parks are also covered. Rent regulation excludes condominium and townhome tenancies commencing after December 31, 1995. The market-rate allowance is conditional on one of the tenant departure, eviction or buyout events specified in the requirement. Applicable RSO exemptions must be resolved, including the incompletely described luxury and temporary exemptions.
rules.exemptions: Nonpayment, a lease violation or failure to comply with a Tenant Habitability Plan must result in eviction to satisfy the corresponding listed trigger. The passage does not authorize a market-rate reset for every eviction.
rules.citation: City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO)

rules.title: Monthly Systematic Code Enforcement Fee pass-through
rules.requirement: A landlord may collect from the rental unit's tenant each month one-twelfth of 50% of the annual Systematic Code Enforcement Fee.
rules.key_value: Monthly: 1/12 of 50% of the annual fee
rules.coverage_conditions: The overview places this allowance within its RSO rent-increase provisions. Its stated RSO scope generally covers Los Angeles rental properties first built on or before October 1, 1978, or replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28, of these types: apartments, condominiums, townhomes, duplexes, two or more single-family dwellings on the same parcel, hotel/motel/rooming-house/boarding-house rooms occupied by the same tenant for more than 30 consecutive days, residential units attached to commercial buildings, ADUs and JADUs. Mobile homes and recreational vehicles in mobile home parks are also covered. Condominium and townhome rent amounts are not regulated for tenancies commencing after December 31, 1995; the overview does not resolve whether that exclusion affects this fee allowance. Applicable luxury and temporary exemptions and the fee's independent coverage require review.
rules.exemptions: The allowance concerns the annual Systematic Code Enforcement Fee; the source does not supply its amount or establish independent fee-assessment coverage.
rules.citation: City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO); Ord. No. 187,108
rules.quoted_span: Effective January 1, 2022, a landlord may collect 1/12 of 50% of the annual Systematic Code Enforcement Fee from the tenant of the rental unit per month. (Added by Ord. No. 187,108, Eff. 8/6/21.)

rules.title: Detector installation surcharge
rules.requirement: Landlords may add a $3.00 rent surcharge for the installation and cost of a hard-wired smoke detector or a combination smoke/carbon monoxide detector.
rules.coverage_conditions: Los Angeles rental properties generally covered by the RSO: first built on or before October 1, 1978, or replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28, with one of the listed types: apartment, condominium, townhome, duplex, two or more single-family dwellings on the same parcel, hotel/motel/rooming-house/boarding-house rooms occupied by the same tenant for more than 30 consecutive days, residential units attached to commercial buildings, ADUs or JADUs. Mobile homes and recreational vehicles in mobile home parks are also covered. Rent regulation excludes condominium and townhome tenancies commencing after December 31, 1995. This allowance concerns installation and cost of the specified detector. Applicable RSO exemptions must be resolved, including the incompletely described luxury and temporary exemptions.
rules.exemptions: The source does not state the surcharge's collection frequency or duration.
rules.citation: City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO)
rules.quoted_span:
A $3.00 surcharge may be added to the rent for the installation and cost of a hard-wired
smoke detector
or a combination smoke/
carbon monoxide detector

rules.title: LAHD approval for specified rent-increase programs
rules.requirement: Landlords must obtain LAHD approval for rent increases under the Capital Improvement, Primary Renovation, Seismic Retrofit, Rehabilitation, and Just and Reasonable Rent Increase programs, subject to the stated program qualifications.
rules.coverage_conditions: Los Angeles rental properties generally covered by the RSO: first built on or before October 1, 1978, or replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28, with one of the listed types: apartment, condominium, townhome, duplex, two or more single-family dwellings on the same parcel, hotel/motel/rooming-house/boarding-house rooms occupied by the same tenant for more than 30 consecutive days, residential units attached to commercial buildings, ADUs or JADUs. Mobile homes and recreational vehicles in mobile home parks are also covered. Rent regulation excludes condominium and townhome tenancies commencing after December 31, 1995. Applicable RSO exemptions must be resolved, including the incompletely described luxury and temporary exemptions. The approval requirement concerns only the listed programs: tenant-benefiting unit or common-area improvements lasting at least five years; major building-system renovations or reduction of hazardous-material exposure; seismic work mandated by Soft-Story Ordinance No. 183893; unit or common-area work complying with an LAHD or other government order; or inflation-adjusted net operating income insufficient to cover property operating expenses.
rules.exemptions: Capital Improvement recovery is for unit or common-area improvements benefiting the tenant and lasting at least five years. Primary Renovation recovery is for major building-system renovations or reducing exposure to hazardous materials. Seismic Retrofit recovery is for work mandated by Soft-Story Ordinance No. 183893. Rehabilitation recovery is for unit or common-area work complying with an LAHD or other government order. A Just and Reasonable application requires inflation-adjusted net operating income insufficient to cover the property's operating expenses.
rules.citation: City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO); RAC Reg 210; RAC Reg 220; Soft-Story Ordinance No. 183893; RAC Reg 250; RAC Reg 240
rules.quoted_span:
Rent increases that require LAHD approval
Capital Improvement Program
: Landlords can recover costs for improvements to the rental unit or common areas for items that benefit the tenant and will last at least five years (
RAC Reg 210
).
Primary Renovation Program
: Landlords can recover costs for major renovations of building systems or to reduce exposure to hazardous materials
(RAC Reg 220).
Seismic Retrofit Program
: Landlords can recover costs for seismic retrofit work mandated by Soft-Story Ordinance No. 183893.
Rehabilitation Program
: Landlords can recover costs for work in a unit or common area to comply with an order issued by LAHD or other government entities (
RAC Reg 250
).
Just and Reasonable Rent Increase
: A landlord can apply for a rent increase when their net operating income adjusted for inflation is not sufficient to cover the property’s operating expenses (
RAC Reg 240
).

rules.title: RSO legal reasons for eviction
rules.requirement: Landlords must base an RSO eviction on a listed legal reason, including the specified tenant-fault grounds or owner/family occupancy, resident-manager occupancy, demolition and permanent removal from the rental market, a government order, or conversion to affordable housing.
rules.coverage_conditions: Los Angeles rental properties generally covered by the RSO: first built on or before October 1, 1978, or replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28, with one of the listed types: apartment, condominium, townhome, duplex, two or more single-family dwellings on the same parcel, hotel/motel/rooming-house/boarding-house rooms occupied by the same tenant for more than 30 consecutive days, residential units attached to commercial buildings, ADUs or JADUs. Mobile homes and recreational vehicles in mobile home parks are also covered. The condominium and townhome exception for tenancies commencing after December 31, 1995 addresses rent amounts and is not stated to exclude eviction protections. Applicable RSO exemptions require review, including whether and how the incompletely described luxury and temporary exemptions affect eviction protections.
rules.exemptions: Listed tenant-fault grounds are failure to pay rent; failure to fix or address a rental-agreement violation; nuisance or damage to the rental unit; illegal use of the unit; failure to renew a similar rental agreement; failure to provide reasonable landlord access; and an unapproved subtenant remaining at the end of the lease term. The owner-occupancy ground extends to an immediate family member. Additional procedures and qualifications are not fully stated in the overview.
rules.citation: City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO)
rules.quoted_span:
Legal Reasons for Eviction
Tenant is at-fault
Failure to pay rent
Failure to fix or address a violation of the rental agreement
Creating a nuisance or causing damage to the rental unit
Using the rental unit for an illegal purpose
Failure to renew a similar rental agreement
Failure to provide the landlord with reasonable access to the rental unit
The person at the end of the lease term is a subtenant not approved by the landlord
Tenant is not at-fault
The owner or immediate family member will move into the rental unit
A resident manager will move into the rental unit
Demolition and permanent removal from the rental market
Government order
Conversion to affordable housing

rules.title: File termination notices with LAHD
rules.requirement: Landlords must file notices terminating tenancies in RSO rental units with LAHD within three business days after service on the tenant.
rules.coverage_conditions: Los Angeles rental properties generally covered by the RSO: first built on or before October 1, 1978, or replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28, with one of the listed types: apartment, condominium, townhome, duplex, two or more single-family dwellings on the same parcel, hotel/motel/rooming-house/boarding-house rooms occupied by the same tenant for more than 30 consecutive days, residential units attached to commercial buildings, ADUs or JADUs. Mobile homes and recreational vehicles in mobile home parks are also covered. The condominium and townhome exception for tenancies commencing after December 31, 1995 addresses rent amounts and is not stated to exclude eviction protections. Applicable RSO exemptions require review, including whether and how the incompletely described luxury and temporary exemptions affect this filing duty.
rules.exemptions: The operative sentence covers all notices terminating tenancies for RSO rental units. Its citation to an additional municipal-code provision does not by itself establish broader address coverage.
rules.quoted_span:
All notices to terminate a tenancy for all rental units subject to
City’s Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO
) must be filed with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) within
three (3) business days of service on the tenant
per Los Angeles Municipal Code 151.09.C.9 & 165.05.B.5.

rules.title: Relocation assistance for no-fault eviction
rules.requirement: Landlords carrying out a no-fault eviction must pay tenant relocation assistance.
rules.key_value: Relocation assistance required; amount not supplied
rules.coverage_conditions: Los Angeles rental properties generally covered by the RSO: first built on or before October 1, 1978, or replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28, with one of the listed types: apartment, condominium, townhome, duplex, two or more single-family dwellings on the same parcel, hotel/motel/rooming-house/boarding-house rooms occupied by the same tenant for more than 30 consecutive days, residential units attached to commercial buildings, ADUs or JADUs. Mobile homes and recreational vehicles in mobile home parks are also covered. The condominium and townhome exception for tenancies commencing after December 31, 1995 addresses rent amounts and is not stated to exclude eviction protections. The payment duty is triggered by a no-fault eviction. Applicable RSO exemptions require review, including whether and how the incompletely described luxury and temporary exemptions affect relocation assistance.
rules.exemptions: The overview lists these no-fault reasons: occupancy by the owner or an immediate family member; occupancy by a resident manager; demolition and permanent removal from the rental market; government order; and conversion to affordable housing. It does not provide assistance amounts, payment timing or more detailed eligibility qualifications.
rules.citation: City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO)

No-fault evictions require the payment of
relocation assistance

rules.title: Declaration for no-fault eviction
rules.requirement: Landlords carrying out a no-fault eviction must file a Landlord Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD.
rules.coverage_conditions: Los Angeles rental properties generally covered by the RSO: first built on or before October 1, 1978, or replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28, with one of the listed types: apartment, condominium, townhome, duplex, two or more single-family dwellings on the same parcel, hotel/motel/rooming-house/boarding-house rooms occupied by the same tenant for more than 30 consecutive days, residential units attached to commercial buildings, ADUs or JADUs. Mobile homes and recreational vehicles in mobile home parks are also covered. The condominium and townhome exception for tenancies commencing after December 31, 1995 addresses rent amounts and is not stated to exclude eviction protections. The declaration duty is triggered by a no-fault eviction. rules.exemptions: The overview lists these no-fault reasons: occupancy by the owner or an immediate family member; occupancy by a resident manager; demolition and permanent removal from the rental market; government order; and conversion to affordable housing. It does not state a declaration-filing deadline.

rules.title: Notice of Right to Counsel
rules.requirement: Landlords must post the Notice of Right to Counsel and provide it to the tenant at the start of the tenancy. They must also attach it to a copy of any eviction notice or termination of a rental subsidy.
rules.key_value: Posting, delivery at tenancy start, and notice attachment
rules.coverage_conditions: The duty appears under the heading for RSO rental units. The overview generally covers Los Angeles rental properties first built on or before October 1, 1978, or replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28, of these types: apartments, condominiums, townhomes, duplexes, two or more single-family dwellings on the same parcel, hotel/motel/rooming-house/boarding-house rooms occupied by the same tenant for more than 30 consecutive days, residential units attached to commercial buildings, ADUs and JADUs. Mobile homes and recreational vehicles in mobile home parks are also covered. The condominium and townhome post-December 31, 1995 tenancy exception addresses rent amounts, not this notice. The sentence itself refers generally to landlords, so any broader coverage and the effect of incompletely described luxury and temporary exemptions require review.
rules.exemptions: The attachment requirement applies to any eviction notice or termination of a rental subsidy. The source does not state that eligibility to receive legal representation limits the notice duty.
rules.citation: City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) overview, Required Registration and Posted Notification of RSO Rental Units
rules.quoted_span:
Beginning August 20, 2025, landlords must post the
Notice of Right to Counsel
and provide it to the tenant at the start of the tenancy. The Notice must also be attached to a copy of any eviction notice or termination of a rental subsidy.

review.issue: All extracted rules require scope review. The overview describes RSO coverage only generally; the allowed facts cannot fully express the listed property types, replacement-unit status, same-parcel dwelling configuration, exact construction cutoff, hotel occupancy in consecutive days, or condominium/townhome tenancy commencement cutoff. Missing address values alone are not the reason for prose coverage.
review.quoted_span:
Generally, the RSO applies to rental properties that were first built on or before October 1, 1978, as well as replacement units under
LAMC Section 151.28
and if any of the following:
Apartment
Condominium (Rent amount is not regulated for tenancies that commenced after December 31, 1995)
Townhome (Rent amount is not regulated for tenancies that commenced after December 31, 1995)
Duplex
Two or more single-family dwelling units on the same parcel
Rooms in a hotel, motel, rooming house, or boarding house occupied by the same tenant for more than 30 consecutive days
Residential unit(s) attached to a commercial building
Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU)
Junior Accessory Dwelling Unit (JADU)
Mobile homes
and recreational vehicles in mobile home parks are also covered under the RSO.

review.issue: The luxury exemption is materially incomplete: the source supplies a historical rent date but omits the qualifying amount or other completed criterion. Do not infer exemption eligibility or its effect on particular RSO protections.
review.quoted_span:
Luxury Exemption
: A landlord can apply for an exemption from the RSO if they can establish the monthly rent charged on or before May 31, 1978,*.

review.issue: Temporary exemptions are referenced without their eligibility criteria or substantive reach. Their effect on address-level coverage cannot be determined from this source.

All units rented or offered for rent must be
registered annually
with LAHD. New property owners have 45 days to register their rental property and if applicable, file
Temporary exemptions

review.issue: The current allowable annual percentage is contained in an uncaptured linked PDF. The overview supports the 12-month frequency rule but does not establish a numeric annual cap.

Precise operative start dates are not supplied for d041-annual-increase-frequency, d041-additional-tenant-increase, d041-market-rate-reset, d041-detector-surcharge, d041-program-increase-approval, d041-eviction-grounds, d041-termination-notice-filing, d041-no-fault-relocation or d041-no-fault-declaration. Their effective_date values remain null; the webpage's modification date is not an effective date.

February 2, 2026 expressly dates the dependent-increase prohibition. It does not unambiguously establish when the continuing allowance for additional nondependent tenants began. The treatment of unauthorized occupants from March 2020 through December 2023 includes a past notice deadline that must not be converted into a current notice opportunity.

Rent increases for unauthorized additional tenants who moved between March 2020 and December 2023 must be provided an advance written notice of rental increase on or before March 1, 2024.

review.issue: The registration-fee passage calls both $1.61 monthly and $38.75 a surcharge, while also allowing a 50% fee pass-through. The relationship among the annual fee, surcharge and current amount is not clear enough to extract a faithful monetary rule. The stated 30-day notice is tied to collecting the $1.61 surcharge.

A $1.61 monthly surcharge may be collected by the landlord as the tenant’s portion of the
Registration
fee. Effective January 1, 2020, the surcharge is $38.75. The landlord may pass through 50% of the fee to the tenant every month rather than once a year.  A 30-day notice must be given to the tenant to collect a rental surcharge of $1.61.

review.issue: The Systematic Code Enforcement Fee passage provides a January 1, 2022 operative date, distinct from the ordinance's August 6, 2021 effective date. Its independent assessment coverage and applicability to units excluded from rent-amount regulation are not established here.
review.quoted_span: Effective January 1, 2022, a landlord may collect 1/12 of 50% of the annual Systematic Code Enforcement Fee from the tenant of the rental unit per month. (Added by Ord. No. 187,108, Eff. 8/6/21.)

review.issue: The overview does not explain how market-rate resets, ordinary annual increases, additional-tenant increases, detector surcharges, fee pass-throughs and approved program increases interact. No precedence or conflict relationship is established.

The no-fault notice checklist says '30-day and 60-day' and mentions 120-day notices or an extension of up to one year without identifying the applicable eviction types or tenant qualifications. A faithful conditional notice-period rule cannot be extracted.
review.quoted_span: Give the tenant a 30-day and 60-day written notice (some evictions require 120-day notice or up to a 1-year extension).

review.issue: Relocation assistance is expressly required for no-fault evictions, but its amount, payment timing and any further eligibility qualifications are not supplied. The source does not establish an additional penalty or damages remedy.

No-fault evictions require the payment of
relocation assistance
.

If My Property is Not Rent Stabilized
